audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart said Skill/Singed/Singed/Skill/Skill/Singed/Singed, giving Singed level 2 and calling 4-6 even. Warwick owns levels 1-2 outright and Singed owns 4 onward.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast (Q) is a 365-range lunge on 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s that heals Warwick for the damage dealt, and Eternal Hunger (P) heals him again under 50% HP. Singed has only Poison Trail at 1 and no Mega Adhesive until 3, so there is no answer to the Q lunge for two levels. Once the proxy game starts at 4-5 and Insanity Potion lands at 6, Warwick has no way to stop it.
audit.corrected: Warwick / Warwick / Skill / Singed / Singed / Singed / Singed — matches the packet chart and the 55.5% Singed win rate over 982 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text credited Warwick's early sustain to a 'Blood Hunt passive'. Blood Hunt is his W, an active on an 80/70/60/50/40s cooldown; the passive is Eternal Hunger.
audit.why: Naming the wrong ability makes the spike untrackable — a player looking for a passive will never watch the 80s W cooldown that actually gates his chase speed.
audit.corrected: Spikes: Warwick lvl 1-2 (Eternal Hunger + Q lunge heal), Singed lvl 3 (Mega Adhesive grounding), lvl 6 (Insanity Potion regen holds you over the 50% HP line both Eternal Hunger and Blood Hunt key off), first item (Rylai's), and every Infinite Duress cooldown window (110/90/70s).

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Mega Adhesive grounds. Both of Warwick's mobility tools — Jaws of the Beast (Q) and Infinite Duress (R) — are leaps, and grounding shuts both off. Separately, the text told you to 'Fling out of' Infinite Duress, which is impossible: suppression stops you acting for its full 1.5s. Primal Howl (E) — 2.5s damage reduction then a 1s flee, 15/14/13/12/11s — was absent entirely despite being the one tool that breaks Singed's run-at pattern.
audit.why: Grounding vs a champion whose entire threat is two leaps is the matchup. Telling a player to Fling during a suppression teaches an input they physically cannot make and costs them the fight.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive grounds Warwick: he cannot Q-lunge or R-leap into or out of the goo. Infinite Duress's leap distance scales with his bonus move speed, so with Blood Hunt active it crosses far more ground than expected. You cannot act during the 1.5s suppression — Fling only after it ends. Primal Howl fears you for 1s and gives him 2.5s of damage reduction; never chase with your back to his tower while it is up. Jaws of the Beast deals max-health damage, so raw armour is the wrong answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldown advice named Infinite Duress but never gave a number.
audit.why: 'Track his R' is unactionable without the duration of the window it opens.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70s. At rank 1 that is a 110-second window where Warwick has no kill pressure at all — that is your proxy and dive window, not a moment to farm safe.

audit.why: Anti-heal is already core in the build text, which is right — Jaws of the Beast and Eternal Hunger are both heals, and Insanity Potion applies Grievous Wounds through Poison Trail.

edits.after: Proxy time: Warwick cannot stop you farming behind his wave, and Eternal Hunger's heal and Blood Hunt's chase speed both switch on only below 50% HP — Insanity Potion's regen holds you above that line.

edits.before: Warwick out-sustains you at levels 1-2 — his Q heal and passive regen eat your Poison Trail damage faster than it accumulates, so don't run into him hoping for a war of attrition. Last-hit from trail range and refuse his face-fights. The moment Fling comes online at level 2, you have a deterrent: if he steps forward to Q you, you can Fling him backward and lap him in poison on the retreat, but don't commit to a full trade while his Q is up and your trail hasn't chunked him first.
edits.after: Warwick out-sustains you at levels 1-2 — Jaws of the Beast heals him for the damage it deals and Eternal Hunger tops him up under 50% HP, so a war of attrition loses. Last-hit from trail range and refuse his face-fights. Fling at level 2 is your deterrent: when he spends the 8s Q lunge to step in, Fling him backward and lap him in poison on the retreat. Primal Howl fears you for 1 second on a 15s cooldown, so never chase him with your back to his tower.

edits.before: Level 3 Mega Adhesive changes the dynamic — drop glue to root him in your Poison Trail if he tries to close, and he cannot Q-drain his way out because you keep moving. From levels 4-5 start proxying: run behind his tower, lay Poison Trail, and force him to choose between losing CS or chasing you into the fog. He is not mobile enough to hunt you down efficiently, and every time he commits to a chase he bleeds out in your cloud. At level 6, Insanity Potion gives you the stat dump that makes him a passenger — his Blood Hunt passive needs you to be low-HP to activate fully, and R keeps you healthy enough to deny that trigger.
edits.after: Level 3 Mega Adhesive changes the dynamic — the goo grounds him, so Jaws of the Beast cannot lunge him into or out of it, and anyone you Fling into that glue is rooted outright. From levels 4-5 start proxying: run behind his tower, lay Poison Trail, and force him to choose between losing CS or chasing you into the fog. Every chase he commits to bleeds him out in your cloud, and a Fling that lands him in the glue roots him for a full extra lap of poison. At level 6, Insanity Potion makes him a passenger — Eternal Hunger and Blood Hunt only switch on under 50% HP, and R's regen keeps you over that line.

edits.before: Warwick's only win condition after first item is landing Infinite Duress, so track it the way you track any point-and-click suppression: if you see him sprint toward you with Blood Hunt active and R up, respect the engage or pre-empt it with Mega Adhesive to slow his approach and force him to eat your poison before he ever reaches you. Once R is on cooldown he is helpless — run the Poison Trail through him, Fling him back into the wave, and repeat. In a full side-lane split he cannot duel a two-item Singed who keeps Insanity Potion for the commit; his sustain does not keep pace with a persistent Rylai's-slowed poison cloud, and he lacks the mobility to disengage once you choose to run at him.
edits.after: Warwick's only win condition after first item is landing Infinite Duress, and its leap distance scales with his bonus move speed — with Blood Hunt running it crosses far more ground than you expect, so pre-empt it with Mega Adhesive: grounded, he cannot leap at all and has to walk through your poison. Once R is down he is helpless for 90 seconds at rank 2 — run Poison Trail through him, Fling him back into the wave, and repeat. Primal Howl's 1s fear is his only way off the chase — walk him into burning it early. In a side-lane split he cannot duel a two-item Singed holding Insanity Potion for the commit; his sustain never keeps pace with a Rylai's-slowed cloud.

notes: All 2 suspectNames for this matchup are false positives — 'Run Poison Trail' and 'Land Infinite Duress' are correct Riot names, the matcher tripped on the leading verb. The real name defect the scanner missed is 'Blood Hunt passive', used three times: Blood Hunt is Warwick's W active (80/70/60/50/40s), his passive is Eternal Hunger. Level chart was flipped to match the packet chart as an atomic group across both layers.
